title: A container says when it is hiding something you drew
goal: When a card or a screen is set to cut off what does not fit, anything that ends up outside its edge simply vanishes, with nothing anywhere saying it is still there. Somebody who drags a label a little too far loses it and has no way back but undo. The layer should say, where you can see it, that it is being hidden by the box it lives in.
notes: Comes from the rough list of queue/audits/2026-09-05-clip-contents.json. Layer.clipsToBounds and Layer.localBounds are the two facts needed: a child is out of view when its own localBounds does not intersect the parent's. The Layers list rows are built in Sources/Photonz/LayersPanel.swift; the hidden and locked marks already there are the pattern to follow. Applies to frames too, which have had this gap since frames landed. DONE: RowOutOfView.swift + LayerPanelTree.layerRows(marksOutOfView:) in PhotonzCore; OutOfViewMark in LayersPanel.swift; audit queue/audits/2026-09-06-out-of-view.json; walks out-of-view-mark-walk.json and out-of-view-screen-walk.json.
acceptance: A layer that is fully outside its clipping container is marked as hidden in the Layers list, in a way you can see without hovering
The mark says why in plain words when you hover it, naming the container that is cutting it off
Selecting that layer still shows its position, so you can type it back into view
Nothing is marked while its container is not cutting anything off
Ships behind next-auto-layout, and covers a screen as well as a group

log.note: Adversarial review BEFORE building. Walked it as a first-timer: they drag a label out of a clipping card, it vanishes, they look at the Layers list. The row is the right place, because it is the only surface that lists a layer you cannot see. Three things the task did not say: (1) the mark is useless while its group is SHUT, and a shut group is exactly the state somebody is in after collapsing a card, so the shut container has to speak too; (2) marking a layer that is HALF out would fire on every card whose title runs a little wide, so only a layer completely outside is marked; (3) naming the OUTERMOST container would send somebody to the wrong box, so the nearest one is named. Cut from the idea: no canvas chrome, no ghost outline where the layer went, no badge count on the container beyond a plain sentence in the tip. The shortest thing that delivers the value is one mark on the row plus a tip that names the box.

Core, TDD: RowOutOfView + OutOfView in Sources/PhotonzCore/RowOutOfView.swift, carried on LayerRowDisplay.outOfView and worked out in one pass inside PhotonzDocument.layerRows (Sources/PhotonzCore/LayerPanelTree.swift). Clip boxes travel down the walk as ClipScope values already in the child's coordinate space, so nesting costs nothing extra. 'Outside' compares edges rather than using CGRect.intersects, because a flat arrow or a one-point divider is an EMPTY rect that intersects nothing and would otherwise be marked. A box is only worked out under a container that is already cutting or on a container that cuts, so a document that clips nothing costs exactly what it always did. 14 tests in Tests/PhotonzCoreTests/OutOfViewMarkTests.swift.

App: OutOfViewMark in Sources/Photonz/LayersPanel.swift, an orange scissors beside the name (same slot as the component mark, because it is part of what the row IS). Gated through EditorState.layerRows on Experiments.shared.autoLayoutEnabled (next-auto-layout). The row's playtest detail now carries the mark so a walk can read it.

Verified on the real app, Screen Recording granted so these are real captures. Scripts/playtest/out-of-view-mark-walk.json: card held to 120 and clipped, shut Card row marked, opening it moves the mark to Body alone (Title/Picture/Background clean), unticking clears every mark. Scripts/playtest/out-of-view-screen-walk.json: a rectangle typed to Y 900 inside a screen is marked, Y still reads 900 as a typeable field, typing it back clears the mark. Full suite 3751 tests green.

Adversarial review AFTER building. What still feels clumsy, all in the audit's rough: there is no one-click way back (the tip tells you to move it or untick the switch), the mark lives in the Layers list only so a collapsed dock says nothing, and the flag gate means a screen still says nothing with next-auto-layout off even though screens have clipped since they landed.
